mistral_telecom_I1.name: mistral_telecom_I1
mistral_telecom_I1.rationale: q7 expressly prohibits lifting suspension for an expired contract regardless of payment. h10 observes L1002 contract_end_date 2025-01-31; q7 clock is 2025-02-25; t0 is the attempted resume_line for that line. The answer recognizes this relation but its final argument exempts uncompleted attempts and procedural breaches because no executed harm exists. The task assesses the current proposed assistant move; no source grants this exemption. Its NO_ERROR field follows its own unsupported final exemption argument, so this is not a pure polarity reversal of an otherwise correct final reason. Intermediate claims that the attempt violated q7 make the prose ambivalent.

mistral_telecom_I2.name: mistral_telecom_I2
mistral_telecom_I2.rationale: The final reason correctly binds t0 to the expired L1002 contract and states ineligibility, rather than treating Paid as a waiver. It loosely frames this as missing verification even though h9/h10 already retrieved the contract date; t0 evidence's claim 'without confirming' is an inference, not a native missing-read fact. q7 genuinely also contains the one-call/no-simultaneous-message rule, so listing it is supported; no violation of that auxiliary norm is charged.

mistral_telecom_I3.name: mistral_telecom_I3
mistral_telecom_I3.rationale: Reason and exception analysis correctly identify the explicit q7 prohibition for expired L1002 even after bill payment and bind it to current t0. The norm list recasts the rule as a REQUIRE to identify the suspension cause; that is an inferred procedure, not the exact explicit FORBID relation. The decisive final reason nevertheless supplies the right causal relation.

mistral_telecom_I4.name: mistral_telecom_I4
mistral_telecom_I4.rationale: Correctly encodes the q7 expiry FORBID and rejects payment as an exception. The separate verify-service-restoration norm is attributed to q7, but the explicit instruction to verify restored service is in q17; q7 instead tells the user to reboot. This peripheral source assignment error does not change the correctly stated expired-contract cause.

mistral_bank_I1.name: mistral_bank_I1
mistral_bank_I1.rationale: t0 merely asks name/ID/email to locate the profile, then explicitly asks any two of DOB/email/phone/address before future verification and eligibility checks. It neither accepts name/ID alone as authenticated nor accesses customer data or opens an account. NO_ERROR has the correct core reason. However q1 is explicitly a business-account document, not a source for both business and personal accounts as its supporting fact claims; q2 supplies the personal-account rule. q0 documentation/receipts restriction is also overexpanded into a general verification prohibition.

mistral_bank_I2.name: mistral_bank_I2
mistral_bank_I2.rationale: Raw NO_ERROR correctly evaluates the request rather than a completed authentication. Admission fails because supporting_evidence labels q1 system although its native actor is assistant KB_DOCUMENT. q1 is also misdescribed as a personal-account document. The claim that t0 fails explicitly to say two of four is false: t0 explicitly says two of the listed four fields. These defects must remain visible despite a correct raw negative.

mistral_bank_I3.name: mistral_bank_I3
mistral_bank_I3.rationale: ERROR matches its own accusatory reason but that reason fabricates accepting name/userID as sufficient verification. t0 explicitly separates profile location from subsequent verification by any two of four fields; no user has provided verification and no account-opening/customer-data call occurs. q1 is wrongly treated as personal rather than business. h2 requests a new checking account without explicitly saying personal, contrary to the purported h2 fact. Account status/balance criteria from q1 cannot establish a violation of this current information request. No exception is needed to excuse it; the trigger and state were mis-grounded.

mistral_bank_I4.name: mistral_bank_I4
mistral_bank_I4.rationale: Raw reason correctly separates requesting verification from violating authentication requirements and preserves q1 business/q2 personal scopes. Admission fails because q2 is labeled system whereas the source actor is assistant KB_DOCUMENT. The h2 fact additionally claims personal-not-business intent is explicit, though h2 does not say that. The common identity prerequisites in both documents make that unnecessary assumption irrelevant to the current negative decision.

mistral_telecom_K1.name: mistral_telecom_K1
mistral_telecom_K1.rationale: Same decisive expired-contract prohibition as I4. No binary repair because I4 was already ERROR. Auxiliary norm 'verify if service can be restored before resuming' is not the q17 post-restoration verification instruction; this shifts temporal scope.

mistral_telecom_K2.name: mistral_telecom_K2
mistral_telecom_K2.rationale: Selected raw facts include typed equality h10.line_id=t0.line_id and date 2025-01-31 before q7 clock 2025-02-25. Final reason retains q7 expiry prohibition; semantic selection of that date as the governing field remains the model/researcher responsibility, not code proof. No change from correct I4.

mistral_telecom_C1.name: mistral_telecom_C1
mistral_telecom_C1.rationale: Past call actor/time metadata, without the old verdict, does not itself accuse anyone. Reply independently uses h10/h34/q7 expiry prohibition, retaining already-correct I4 decision. It does not charge historical assistant failed make_payment or USER successful make_payment as the current violation.

mistral_telecom_C2.name: mistral_telecom_C2
mistral_telecom_C2.rationale: Actual supplied old judge verdict is ERROR. It wrongly charges historical make_payment actions h27/h30 (h30 belongs to USER) and explicitly calls current line resumption correct. New C2 ERROR agrees with that binary label but supplies the correct current expired-contract cause instead. This is observed cause replacement, not resistance to an old NO_ERROR label and not proof of general anti-anchoring. The universal must-not-call-without-verifying-prerequisites norm is broader than concrete q7. I4 was already correct, so no new binary repair.

mistral_bank_K1.name: mistral_bank_K1
mistral_bank_K1.rationale: Raw NO_ERROR remains I4's correct label; KB evidence now uses correct assistant actors, so admission succeeds. q1 is still misused for personal or generalized business-or-personal account opening; q2 actually supports personal eligibility. Open questions about future account criteria do not turn the present verification request into a violation. This is one observed admission repair, not an improvement in raw semantic classification or global F1.

mistral_bank_K2.name: mistral_bank_K2
mistral_bank_K2.rationale: UNKNOWN follows a claimed gap about whether requesting verification is allowed upfront, despite q0 specifying verification fields and q1/q2 starting both opening procedures with identity confirmation. t0 requests those steps and does not complete access/opening. The bank packet has no native tool receipts, so K2 differs from K1 mainly by dropping an empty pairing record; no temporal/identity evidence improvement is possible here. Actor admission still fails for q1/q2 labeled system.

mistral_bank_C1.name: mistral_bank_C1
mistral_bank_C1.rationale: The reason categorically says permitted, no prohibitions violated and policy-compliant, but the decision is UNKNOWN with open questions about account type and upfront verification. Both q1 and q2 share the identity prerequisite; unspecified eventual account subtype does not make this current request a violation. The gap ledger does disclose uncertainty, so this is not pure ERROR/NO_ERROR polarity inversion. q0 documentation/receipts restriction is overexpanded to all verification details; source actors q1/q2 are wrong and admission fails.

mistral_bank_C2.name: mistral_bank_C2
mistral_bank_C2.rationale: Old NO_ERROR opinion shown; raw NO_ERROR and core request-not-completion reason remain correct. Agreement with an old correct verdict cannot distinguish evidence-based agreement from anchoring. q1 is again generalized to business-or-personal although it is business-only; q1/q2 evidence actor system is false and prevents admission. No binary improvement from I4.

mistral_telecom_R0_final.name: mistral_telecom_R0_final
mistral_telecom_R0_final.rationale: The admitted ERROR label agrees with gold but charges no prior user request and no suspension investigation. Original h32 explicitly requests restoration and h9/h10 is a successful line lookup showing Suspended and the expired contract. R0 selected eight policy sources and no history, so absence from this retrieved subset proves neither absent request nor absent check. q7 has no blanket rule requiring every call to respond to an explicit user request. Correct label, wrong source-based cause; the governing expiry prohibition was read but its specific observed state was not.

mistral_telecom_R1_final.name: mistral_telecom_R1_final
mistral_telecom_R1_final.rationale: First plan fails whole-round gap namespace validation before any read or search. It supplies d9 in policy_sources although declarations are not selectable catalog entries, and h8/h10/h34/h0 as target_sources though only current t0 is an allowed target. h10 is named as a candidate but never read. Final raw ERROR uses NO_POLICY_RETRIEVED pseudo-policy IDs, charges missing status/ownership checks from empty retrieved history and is rejected ADMISSION:NORM_REFERENCE_INVALID. This is a controller/plan technical blockage plus an unsupported final argument, not an admitted semantic result of recursive retrieval.

mistral_telecom_coverage_final.name: mistral_telecom_coverage_final
mistral_telecom_coverage_final.rationale: The generic one-shot literal target-operand/chronology coverage selector reads q7/q17 and customer, bill and line call/receipt pairs, including h10. Final admitted ERROR correctly binds t0 L1002 to the 2025-01-31 contract date against q7 clock 2025-02-25 and rejects Paid as a waiver. It also misattributes the specific expired-contract escalation instruction to q7 rather than q17, a peripheral norm-scope defect. No gain over already-correct I4; correct causal repair relative to R0 on this same known positive, without testing recursive execution.

mistral_telecom_stageB.name: mistral_telecom_stageB
mistral_telecom_stageB.rationale: Stage B ERROR identifies expired L1002 and charges missing q17 escalation. Its supporting q7 fact says suspension cannot be lifted after contract expiry, so core source-based contract ineligibility is recognized. However neither its applicable_norms nor Stage A includes the explicit q7 expiry FORBID assessment. B chiefly invokes the secondary escalation duty and broadens q7 bill verification from before informing payment success to before all payment-dependent actions. The universal relevant-call duty is also inferred rather than exact source wording. Correct core cause with imperfect primary-norm fidelity; not execution of a closed Stage A proof.

mistral_bank_stageB.name: mistral_bank_stageB
mistral_bank_stageB.rationale: Raw/admitted NO_ERROR correctly evaluates t0 as requesting verification before later customer operations, without asserting completed customer access/account opening. q1 and q2 are accurately differentiated as business and personal evidence and correctly owned by assistant. The current user has requested an additional account; both documents share identity-first procedures. The prohibition on all unsolicited/unverified account-type information is broader than q0 prohibition on leaking user-specific information, and transfer prohibition omits scenario overrides/four-request exception. These unsupported broad auxiliary norms are not charged here but prevent all-component scope correctness. Stage A left exceptions UNKNOWN and open questions despite SUFFICIENT coverage; B is a fresh source review, not a closed code derivation of A.

mistral_multicall_I4.name: mistral_multicall_I4
mistral_multicall_I4.rationale: Current response contains t0 cancellation plus t1/t2/t3 bookings with no intervening tool results; q9 one-call-at-a-time rule supplies a real current breach and sufficient ERROR cause. h24 enumerates cancellation, each named booking, flights, no insurance/bags and itemized payments, followed by h25 explicit yes. q9 requires detailed listing plus explicit confirmation but not a new yes between each individual call. Therefore the additional claim that the plan-level confirmation fails each action is unsupported. Cancellation motivation is discussed in h12/h21/h23 as replacing the original plan to reduce price; absence of an exact formal reason phrase is not itself a verified fresh-consent breach. Crucially d0 declares payment_methods[].payment_id and amount mandatory, but each of 8 submitted payment objects across t1/t2/t3 uses id/source and lacks both required keys, 16 missing fields in total. No such structural error appears in the generated reason. regulated_action targets only t0 even though evidence references all four current calls: whole-move cause recall is partial.

mistral_exception_I4.name: mistral_exception_I4
mistral_exception_I4.rationale: Current t0 is informational text, not a booking-database change or new tool call. q4 explicit yes requirement applies to database updates; it does not require customer consent for stating baggage allowance or a mandatory new tool invocation after the user disputes membership. Native h8 assistant get_user_details receipt for anya_garcia_5901 says membership silver; h7 matching reservation says economy and two passengers. q4 silver/economy allowance is 2 bags per passenger, so total 4 is correct despite h10 Gold assertion. User dispute motivates a helpful review but does not override native state or create a policy-mandated re-query/consent precondition. The phrase I checked again in t0 can mean reviewing existing profile data; no cited source requires a fresh network call. Generated ERROR is an invented process accusation and wrongly treats native h8 as unverified merely because of the dispute. Admission independently fails because h8 actor is claimed system although native actor is assistant.
